A Christ-centered Courtship is a series of messages on godly courtship preached by Paul Hershberger. He preached these messages several times at different locations over the last ten years. Recently, we had them transcribed and abridged for reading clarity. After printing all six articles in The Heartbeat of the Remnant, we will publish them in a booklet. This is the first article of six.

Introduction

My wife and I had the privilege of having a courtship without regrets or guilt. We were blessed with parents who guided us in the right way and gave us opportunities that they didn’t have.

If you don’t have that testimony or memory, please don’t go on a guilt trip. But my prayer for you is that you get a burning burden and vision in your heart to have it for your children. That can be your reward.

A Christ-centered courtship is a period of time between a single life and a married life. The decisions you make in this period will affect you for the rest of your lives. With God’s blessing on your life, you can end up with no regrets or guilt.

Five goals for this Christ-Centered Courtship series.

Goal #1. To turn the hearts of the fathers to their children.

Goal #2. To turn the hearts of the children to their fathers.

Goal #3. That parents would get a burden to lead each one of their children into the perfect will of God for their lives.

Goal #4. That young people would get a burden to seek after God, find fulfillment and purpose in walking with God, and you would seek maturity in your manners and in your character.

Goal #5. That young men and young women would rise up to be godly fathers and godly mothers with a vision to raise up another godly generation, and the Gospel of Jesus Christ can go on.

God’s Plan for Male and Female

Ecclesiastes 12:1 says, “Remember now thy Creator in the days of thy youth, while the evil days come not, nor the years draw nigh, when thou shalt say, I have no pleasure in them.” My desire is that each one of you, remember your Creator in the days of your youth. Turn your heart, your focus, and your life to pursue after your Creator, Almighty God, in heaven.

What does he mean, “while the evil days come not” and “the years draw nigh”? It means to seek the Lord when you’re young. Take the energy of your youth and seek after God. Young people, you’re young and full of ideas, visions, plans, and dreams. I doubt there are any of you who just enjoy sitting down in an easy chair, putting your feet up, and just dreaming about how terrible and horrible life is going to be. We don’t do that, do we? But if we don’t walk with God and follow God’s plan, hard things will come upon us. When hard things come in life, we have no place to turn to. We dream that life will turn out well. The decisions and actions in our youth affect us for the rest of our lives. The good news is they can affect us in a good way. The bad news is they can affect us in a bad way. It depends on what decisions and choices we make. But young people, you’re young, and you have the opportunity to choose.

Let’s go to the beginning of Genesis.

“And the LORD God said, It is not good that the man should be alone; I will make him an help meet for him. And out of the ground the LORD God formed every beast of the field, and every fowl of the air; and brought them unto Adam to see what he would call them: and whatsoever Adam called every living creature, that was the name thereof. And Adam gave names to all cattle, and to the fowl of the air, and to every beast of the field; but for Adam there was not found an help meet for him. And the LORD God caused a deep sleep to fall upon Adam, and he slept: and he took one of his ribs, and closed up the flesh instead thereof; And the rib, which the LORD God had taken from man, made he a woman, and brought her unto the man. And Adam said, This is now bone of my bones, and flesh of my flesh: she shall be called Woman, because she was taken out of Man. Therefore shall a man leave his father and his mother, and shall cleave unto his wife: and they shall be one flesh” (Genesis 2:18-24).

“And God said, Let us make man in our image, after our likeness: and let them have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the fowl of the air, and over the cattle, and over all the earth, and over every creeping thing that creepeth upon the earth. So God created man in his own image, in the image of God created he him; male and female created he them. And God blessed them, and God said unto them, Be fruitful, and multiply, and replenish the earth, and subdue it: and have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the fowl of the air, and over every living thing that moveth upon the earth” (Genesis 1:26-28).

“And the Lord God said, It is not good that the man should be alone; I will make him an help meet for him” (Genesis 2:18). “I’ll make him an help that is meet for him.” God said He would do that.

“So God created man in his own image, in the image of God created he him; male and female created he them” (Genesis 1:27). God made. God created us male and female. It takes a lot of blind faith to believe that we evolved perfectly as male and female. The creation of male and female is God’s plan. It is one of the living proofs of Creation. God made. God created. It’s God’s plan. God is the Author. And God’s plan brings blessing.

I’d like to look at ten different aspects of this blessing of God’s plan.

1) God brings Eve to Adam.

“And the rib, which the Lord God had taken from man, made he a woman, and brought her unto the man. And Adam said, This is now bone of my bones, and flesh of my flesh: she shall be called Woman, because she was taken out of Man” (Genesis 2:22-23).

God caused Adam to fall into a deep sleep. Then God created Eve and brought her to Adam. Adam awoke and realized, “This one is for me!” He had seen all the animals go by when he named them. Now God brings him someone that is for him. He also realized, “She was taken out of my side.” She’s close to his heart. “This is bone of my bones and flesh of my flesh.” It’s not a dog; it’s not a giraffe, or a monkey, or an ape. This one that God brought to him is like him. God’s plan has a blessing.

Adam and Eve had never had a companion before. Adam and Eve had never let the emotions of their heart go before. Something happened in Adam and Eve’s hearts. Adam was a “one-woman man,” and Eve was a “one-man woman.” They never gave their heart passions to anybody else. God has that plan for us, too. God’s plan brings blessings.

2) Leaving and cleaving in unity for life.

“Therefore Bshall a man leave his father and his mother, and shall cleave unto his wife: and they shall be one flesh” (Genesis 2:24).

This verse says, “Therefore shall a man leave his father and his mother,” but Adam and Eve did not have a father and mother. What God is saying it doesn’t work for there to be cleaving unless there’s leaving. Also, in Mark 10:7, we read, “For this cause shall a man leave his father and mother, and cleave to his wife.” This is God’s plan, and God’s plan brings blessing.

Leaving means to leave behind, to abandon. “For this cause shall a man leave his father and mother” is to leave parents leave behind. Let’s consider a young man who has a really good home life. He’s blessed and has everything he needs. Yet once God brings his Eve into his life, something rises up inside him, and he says, “I’m leaving!” But this is God’s plan. And God’s plan brings blessing.

It’s not just leaving his father and mother; he also cleaves to his wife. Cleave means “to glue to, to adhere.” We are very familiar with glued wood panels. All kinds of solid furniture are made out of panels glued together. And if they’re glued together right, they will not come apart at the joints. If you tear them apart, you’re going to have to tear the wood apart. God’s glue is the same way, where it glues two people together. The only way to tear them apart is by splintering and ripping and God does not bless that. But leaving and cleaving, staying together and being glued together, that’s God’s plan and it brings blessing.

3) They shall be one flesh.

“Therefore shall a man leave his father and his mother, and shall cleave unto his wife: and they shall be one flesh” (Genesis 2:24). Two single people who become one married couple, become one unit before God, and become one family before God. They become one flesh, where God sees them as together as one.

“And they twain shall be one flesh: so then they are no more twain, but one flesh. What therefore God hath joined together, let not man put asunder” (Mark 10:8-9). God’s plan for male and female is that He brings Eve to Adam. Then the leaving and cleaving to take place. He causes them to become one flesh. Pulling apart is no blessing at all but bringsagony,pain,travail, and hurt. There is no blessing in separation. But God’s plan brings blessing.

4) Not an unequal yoke.

“Be ye not unequally yoked together with unbelievers: for what fellowship hath righteousness with unrighteousness” (2 Corinthians 6:14-15). “The wife is bound by the law as long as her husband liveth; but if her husband be dead, she is at liberty to be married to whom she will; only in the Lord” (1 Corinthians 7:39).

God’s plan is that marriage is an equal yoke. God will not bring an Eve to an Adam in a marriage that is an unequal yoke.Let’s think about leaving and cleaving, getting glued together, and two becoming one. In marriage, those two are now one before God. Imagine being in a bad marriage relationship like this—a family like this trying to function together. There will be no blessing.

But an equal yoke brings blessing! God desires that we be joined together in one flesh, one heart, and one mind. He wants to see us joined in heart, mind, and fleashthe whole being, being one. God’s plan brings blessing.

5) God planned for us to have children.

“And God blessed them, and God said unto them, Be fruitful, and multiply, and replenish the earth, and subdue it: and have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the fowl of the air, and over every living thing that moveth upon the earth” (Genesis 1:28). Think of the joy and miracle every time another child is born into a Christian home. God planned it this way. And if God brought Adam his Eve, and they leave and cleave, they become one flesh, one heart, one mind. If they are equally yoked and God blesses them with children, it becomes a joyful haven where God can dwell. “And God blessed Noah and his sons, and said unto them, Be fruitful, and multiply, and replenish the earth” (Genesis 9:1). “And you, be ye fruitful, and multiply; bring forth abundantly in the earth, and multiply therein” (Genesis 9:7). God’s plan brings blessing.

6) Headship order.

“But I would have you know, that the head of every man is Christ; and the head of the woman is the man; and the head of Christ is God” (1 Corinthians 11:3). It is God, and then Christ, the man, and the woman. God established a headship order, and this headship order is a blessing. It’s God’s plan, and it’s a blessing.

“Children, obey your parents in the Lord: for this is right. Honor thy father and mother; which is the first commandment with promise; That it may be well with thee, and thou mayest live long on the earth” (Ephesians 6:1-3). . Children, obey your parents in the Lord is a part of the headship order. This not difficult to understand, is it? A home following the plan of God is just a blessed situation. Young people learn to be under authority. Make that your high priority. The sooner you learn to be under authority, the better you will be prepared for the responsibilities in life.

I remember looking at married life and having aspirations about teaching children and raising a godly family. I listened to the “Godly Home” series and thought I was ready to go. But then the day came when it was my turn and my responsibility, and all of a sudden, my heart wanted to wither. Responsibility doesn’t feel the same as dreaming about it does. YOU need to do something! YOU are responsible. YOU need to make it happen. And, by the way, not just make it happen; you need to make it happen in a Christlike way. You need to make it happen in a way that the anointing of the Spirit of God can come down on your family. The better we learn how to be under authority, the better we’ll be prepared for those responsibilities. The more we realize we need God, the better off we are. Let’s make a high priority out of learning to be under authority as children and as young people. “My son, forget not my law; but let thine heart keep my commandments: For length of days, and long life, and peace, shall they add to thee” (Proverbs 3:1-2).

God will add his blessing if we stay in this headship order. The more you learn how to be under authority, the more you will be blessed when you establish your home. God’s plan has blessings.

7) A godly marriage.

Ephesians 5:21,22,24 says, “Submitting yourselves one to another in the fear of God. Wives, submit yourselves unto your own husbands, as unto the Lord. . . Therefore as the church is subject unto Christ, so let the wives be to their own husbands in every thing.”

First of all look at verse 21, “submitting yourselves one to another.” There’s a blending together that needs to happen in a godly home. This blending together should happen in the fear of God. If we’re submitting one to another in the fear of God, we’re going to obey God because we want His blessings.

Ephesians 5: 22, 24 “Wives, submit yourselves unto your own husbands, as unto the Lord. . . Therefore as the church is subject unto Christ, so let the wives be to their own husbands in every thing.” Young ladies, you can count on it: submission to Dad equals submission to a husband. You can practice while you are single. This will help build character in your life. Being a rebellious and froward woman is not going to bring the blessing of God.

It goes on and says, in Ephesians 5:25,28,29. “Husbands, love your wives, even as Christ also loved the church, and gave himself for it . . . So ought men to love their wives as their own bodies. He that loveth his wife loveth himself. For no man ever yet hated his own flesh; but nourisheth and cherisheth it, even as the Lord the church.” Young men, this says that husbands should love their wives. So who do you think God put in your life to prepare you to love your wife? Your mother! Do you want to learn how to love your wife? Learn how to get along with your mom, love your mom, and care about her. Do you want to practice to love your future wife? Go ahead and love your mom.

Verse 33, “Nevertheless let every one of you in particular so love his wife even as himself; and the wife see that she reverence her husband.” God’s plan brings blessings.

8) Being heirs together of the grace of life.

1 Peter 3:7 “Likewise, ye husbands, dwell with them according to knowledge, giving honor unto the wife, as unto the weaker vessel, and as being heirs together of the grace of life; that your prayers be not hindered.” As husbands, we give honor to the wife. She is the weaker vessel and the one that born the children! She’s gone through a lot of traumatic changes in her life. She’s the one that gets worn out and tires sooner.

And he says, “Husbands, dwell with them according to knowledge.”

Young men, learn to understand your mom and your sisters. It will help you after you get married. Don’t conclude that—ah, that’s just women. No, you want the blessing of God. Learn to know and understand them.

“Being heirs together of the grace of life.” God wants us to be heirs together of the grace of life. If we’re not heirs together of the grace of life, can we be heirs separated of the grace of life? I don’t think so. He says we should be heirs together so that our prayers are not hindered. So if we’re heirs separated, could we say our prayers will be hindered? Yes, our prayers will be hindered. Let’s give honor unto the wife as unto the weaker vessel. Every ounce you can gain in this area will only bless you later. It’s worth it. God’s plan brings blessing.

9) A blessed and secure home.

This comes partly out of 1 Peter 3:7, but also from Psalm 144:12 “That our sons may be as plants grown up in their youth; that our daughters may be as corner stones, polished after the similitude of a palace.” The grace of God is on a secure home where there is unity. Where Dad is understanding Mom, where Dad cares about Mom. Dad is ministering and is there to help and guide. He’s there to give direction with a heart of compassion. God’s plan for male and female—God’s plan brings blessings.

10) As Christ and the church.

“Therefore as the church is subject unto Christ, so let the wives be to their own husbands in every thing. Husbands, love your wives, even as Christ also loved the church, and gave himself for it; That he might sanctify and cleanse it with the washing of water by the word, That he might present it to himself a glorious church, not having spot, or wrinkle, or any such thing; but that it should be holy and without blemish. So ought men to love their wives as their own bodies. He that loveth his wife loveth himself. For no man ever yet hated his own flesh; but nourisheth and cherisheth it, even as the Lord the church” (Ephesians 5:24-29).

“Husbands, love your wives, even as Christ also loved the church, and gave Himself for it.” God is looking for men who are willing to give their lives. Single young men, who are willing to answer the call and give their life. This is a high calling of God. It’s the plan of God.

Young men, are you willing to lay down your life, your agenda, and those independent things you like to do? Are you willing to be patient, gentle, and understanding? Are you willing to lose sleep and keep going even when you’re tired? Are you willing to stay calm and not react in stressful circumstances? Are you willing to lead and guide a wife and children, eternal souls, through this life?

But my plea is that you would volunteer and say, “I’m willing to apply myself to the Word of God, the will of God, the plan of God, and I’ll give my life. I’m willing to lay it on the altar.” Jesus gave His life for us, and He’s comparing the marriage with the church and Him.

There’s also a need for mothers who are submissive and yielded to authority. Mothers who do not follow the women’s lib of our day but are rather content to be keepers at home.

Young ladies, are you willing to enlist? Will you give your heart to be guided and led? Are you willing to follow and to cheerfully submit to your authority? Are you willing to serve and be spent for your family? Are you willing to serve and be spent for YOUR family? If you get married someday, it will be YOUR family that you’ll be serving and being spent for. Are you willing to bear pain and discomfort? Are you willing to be a helpmeet, giving yourself for his burden and vision?

But as we look at God’s plan and blessings, you want God’s blessing, young people! But that means you need to make choices accordingly. Rise up and make decisions that will lead to maturity. Maturity comes with the process of seeking after God. Make a commitment in your heart to open yourself to God’s blessings and principles. I encourage you to walk with God, to have a relationship with Jesus Christ, and to do so in humility.

Seek after Christlike character, and do it on purpose. It is so easy for us to just live life however it happens. But if we make decisions on purpose, it will take us somewhere! Those decisions matter. Do things according to God’s plan.

God has a plan for male and female and he has a plan for you.

A Christ-centered Courtship is a series of messages on godly courtship preached by Paul Hershberger. He preached these messages several times at different locations over the last ten years. Recently, we had them transcribed and abridged for reading clarity. After printing all six articles in The Heartbeat of the Remnant, we will publish them in a booklet. This is the first article of six.

Utangulizi

Mimi na mke wangu tulipata baraka ya kuwa na mahusiano ya kabla ya ndoa bila majuto au hatia. Tulibarikiwa na wazazi waliotuelekeza kwa njia sahihi na kutupa fursa ambazo wao hawakuwa nazo.

Kama huna ushuhuda huo au kumbukumbu hiyo, tafadhali usijizize hatia. Lakini maombi yangu kwa ajili yako ni kwamba upate mzigo unaowaka moyoni na maono ya kumwomba Mungu upate hivyo kwa watoto wako. Hiyo inaweza kuwa zawadi yako.

Mahusiano ya kabla ya ndoa yenye Kristo katikati ni kipindi cha wakati kati ya maisha ya mtu asiyeolewa/asiyeolewa na maisha ya ndoa. Maamuzi utakayoifanya katika kipindi hiki yatawadhuru kwa maisha yenu yote. Kwa baraka za Mungu juu ya maisha yenu, mnaweza kumaliza bila majuto wala hatia.

Malisia matano ya mfululizo huu wa Mahusiano yenye Kristo katikati.

Lengo #1. Kurudisha mioyo ya wazazi kwa watoto wao.

Lengo #2. Kurudisha mioyo ya watoto kwa wazazi wao.

Lengo #3. Ili wazazi wapate mzigo wa kuongoza kila mtoto wao katika mapenzi kamili ya Mungu kwa maisha yao.

Lengo #4. Ili vijana wapate mzigo wa kumtafuta Mungu, kupata ukamilifu na kusudi katika kutembea na Mungu, na mttafute ukuaji katika adabu zenu na tabia zenu.

Lengo #5. Ili wavulana na wasichana wamke wapanduke kuwa waume wema na wake wema wenye maono ya kukuzia kizazi kingine kitakatifu, na Injili ya Yesu Kristo iendelee kutangazwa.

Mpango wa Mungu kwa Mwanaume na Mwanamke

Mhubiri 12:1 inasema, "Kumbukeni sasa Muumbaji wenu katika siku za ujana wenu, kabla siku za uovu hazijakuja wala miaka isiwe karibu, mtakaposema, Sina raha kwao." Matarajio yangu ni kwamba kila mmoja wenu akumbuke Muumba wake wakati wa ujana. Geuza moyo wako, umakini wako, na maisha yako kumfuata Muumba wako, Mungu Mwenyezi, mbinguni.

Anamaanisha nini, "wakati siku mbaya hazijakuja" na "miezi/miaka ina karibia"? Inamaanisha kumwomba Bwana ukiwa mchanga. Tumia nguvu za ujana wako kumtafuta Mungu. Vijana, ninyi ni wachanga na mna mawazo, maono, mipango, na ndoto. Shaka zangu ni kwamba hakuna miongoni mwenu anafurahia kukaa kiti cha kupumzika, kupandisha miguu, na kuota tu jinsi maisha yatakavyokuwa mabaya na ya kutisha. Hatuifanyi hivyo, siyo? Lakini tukikutembea bila Mungu na kufuata mpango wa Mungu, mambo magumu yatajiri. Wakati mambo magumu yatufika maishani, hatuna mahali pa kugeukia. Tunaota maisha yatatokea vizuri. Maamuzi na vitendo vya ujana wetu vinatuathiri kwa maisha yote. Habari njema ni kwamba vinaweza kutuathiri kwa njia nzuri. Habari mbaya ni kwamba vinaweza kutuathiri kwa njia mbaya. Inategemea maamuzi na chaguo tunayofanya. Vijana, ninyi ni wachanga, na mna fursa ya kuchagua.

Tuchukue Mwanzo katika Mwanzo.

"Na Mungu Mwenyezi akasema, Si vyema mwanaadamu kuwa peke yake; nitamfanya msaada wake wa mfaa kwa ajili yake. Mungu Akamfanya mnyama wa kila uwanja, na ndege wa angani, akawaleta kwa Adamu kuona yatakayoitwa nini; na vile Adamu alivyoitwa kila kiumbe hai, hiyo ndio jina lake." Na Adamu akamwita majina yote ng'ombe, na ndege wa angani, na kila mnyama wa uwanja; lakini kwa Adamu hakupatikana msaada wake wa mfaa. Basi Bwana Mungu akamfanya Adamu kulala usingizi wa ndani, akalala, akamchukua moja ya upepo wake, akafunga nyama huko badala yake; Na upepo ambao Bwana Mungu alikuwa amemchukua kwa mtu, akamtengeneza mwanamke, akamuleta kwa mtu. Na Adamu akasema, Hii sasa ni mifupa ya mifupa yangu, na nyama ya nyama yangu: itaitwa Mwanamke; kwa maana imechukuliwa kwa Mtu. Ndipo mwanaume atamwacha baba yake na mama yake, akamweka kwa mke wake; nao watakuwa mwili mmoja." (Mwanzo 2:18-24).

"Na Mungu akasema, Nimtengeneze mwanadamu kwa mfano wetu, kwa sura yetu; nao wamimilike kwa samaki wa bahari, na kwa ndege wa angani, na kwa ng'ombe, na kwa nchi yote, na kwa kila mnyama anayekaleta mwilini. Mungu akamuumba mwanadamu kwa sura yake mwenyewe, kwa sura ya Mungu akamwumba; mwanaume na mwanamke akawaunda. Mungu akawaibariki, akawaambia, Uwe wenye matunda, uzidisheni, mkomholee nchi, mkiitawale; na mlikuwa na mamlaka juu ya samaki wa bahari, na ndege wa angani, na kila kiumbe hai kinachotembea juu ya nchi." (Mwanzo 1:26-28).

"Na Bwana Mungu akasema, Si vyema mwanaume kuwa peke yake; nitamfanya msaada wake wa mfaa kwa ajili yake" (Mwanzo 2:18). "Nitamtengeneza msaada wake mfaa kwa ajili yake." Mungu alisema Atafanya hivyo.

"Basi Mungu akamuumba mwanadamu kwa sura yake mwenyewe, kwa sura ya Mungu akamwumba; mwanaume na mwanamke akawaunda" (Mwanzo 1:27). Mungu alitengeneza. Mungu aliumba sisi kama mwanaume na mwanamke. Inahitaji imani yenye uzito kuona kwamba tulibadilika kwa njia ya EVO na kuwa kamili kama mwanaume na mwanamke. Uumbaji wa mwanaume na mwanamke ni mpango wa Mungu. Hii ni moja ya ushahidi hai wa Uumbaji. Mungu alitengeneza. Mungu aliumba. Hilo ni mpango wa Mungu. Mungu ndiye Mwandishi. Na mpango wa Mungu unaleta baraka.

Ningependa kuangalia nyanja kumi tofauti za baraka hii ya mpango wa Mungu.

1) Mungu anamleta Hawa kwa Adamu.

"Na upepo ambao Bwana Mungu alikuwa amemchukua kwa mtu, akamtengeneza mwanamke, akamuleta kwa mtu. Na Adamu akasema, Hii sasa ni mifupa ya mifupa yangu, na nyama ya nyama yangu: itaitwa Mwanamke; kwa maana imechukuliwa kwa Mtu" (Mwanzo 2:22-23).

Mungu akaleta Adamu usingizini wa ndani. Kisha Mungu akamtengeneza Hawa na kumleta kwa Adamu. Adamu alifuata usingizi na akagundua, "Huyu ni wangu!" Alikuwa amewaona wanyama wote wakipita alipowaita majina. Sasa Mungu anamletea mtu ambaye ni kwa ajili yake. Pia aligundua, "Alitolewa upande wangu." Yupo karibu na moyo wake. "Hii ni mifupa ya mifupa yangu na nyama ya nyama yangu." Si mbwa; si twiga, wala sokwe, wala tumbili. Huyu aliyemletea Mungu ni kama yeye. Mpango wa Mungu una baraka.

Adamu na Hawa hawakuwahi kuwa na mwenzake kabla. Adamu na Hawa hawakuwahi kumwonyesha hisia zao kwa mtu mwingine. Kitu kilitokea mioyoni mwao. Adamu alikuwa "mwanaume wa mke mmoja," na Hawa alikuwa "mwanamke wa mume mmoja." Hawakumpa mtu mwingine tamaa za mioyo yao. Mungu pia ana mpango huo kwetu. Mpango wa Mungu unaleta baraka.

2) Kuacha na kushikamana kwa umoja kwa maisha yote.

"Ndipo mwanaume atamwacha baba yake na mama yake, akamweka kwa mke wake; nao watakuwa mwili mmoja" (Mwanzo 2:24).

Betu hii inasema, "Ndipo mwanaume atamwacha baba yake na mama yake," lakini Adamu na Hawa hawakuwa na baba wala mama. Hivyo kile Mungu anachomaanisha ni kwamba haina maana kuwa na kushikamana pasipo kuwa na kuacha. Pia, katika Marko 10:7 tunasoma, "Kwa hiyo mwanaume atamwacha baba yake na mama yake, na atashikamana na mke wake." Huu ni mpango wa Mungu, na mpango wa Mungu unaleta baraka.

Kuacha ina maana ya kuacha nyuma, kuacha. "Kwa ajili hii mwanaume atamwacha baba yake na mama yake" ni kuacha wazazi nyuma. Tuchukulie kijana ambaye ana maisha ya nyumbani mazuri sana. Amebarikiwa na ana kila anachohitaji. Lakini mara Mungu anapoleta Hawa wake maishani mwake, kitu kinaruka ndani yake, na anasema, "Naacha!" Lakini huu ni mpango wa Mungu. Na mpango wa Mungu unaleta baraka.

Sio tu kuacha baba na mama; pia anashikamana na mke wake. Kushikamana kunamaanisha "kushikamana kwa gilu, kuambatana." Tunajua sana paneli za mbao zenye gundi. Aina zote za fanicha ngumu zinatengenezwa kwa paneli ziliogandishwa. Na ikiwa zimengandishwa vizuri, hazitapatana kwa mkutano. Ukiwaza kuzikomboa, utalazimika kuzibomoa mbao. Gundi ya Mungu ni sawa — inagandisha wawili pamoja. Njia pekee ya kuwagawa ni kwa kuzichoma na kuzibomoa na Mungu hakubariki hivyo. Lakini kuacha na kushikamana, kubaki pamoja na kugandishwa pamoja, huo ni mpango wa Mungu na unaleta baraka.

3) Watakuwa mwili mmoja.

"Ndipo mwanaume atamwacha baba yake na mama yake, akamweka kwa mke wake; nao watakuwa mwili mmoja" (Mwanzo 2:24). Watu wawili wasioolewa/waoolewe ambao wanageuka kuwa wanandoa, wanakuwa kitengo kimoja mbele za Mungu, na wanakuwa familia moja mbele za Mungu. Wanakuwa mwili mmoja, ambapo Mungu anawaona pamoja kama mmoja.

"Nao wawili watakuwa mwili mmoja: sasa wao si wawili tena, bali mwili mmoja. Basi kinachochanganya Mungu kimeunganisha, mwanadamu asitoiweke mbali" (Marko 10:8-9). Mpango wa Mungu kwa mwanaume na mwanamke ni kwamba Yeye anamleta Hawa kwa Adamu. Kisha kuachana na kushikamana kutekelezwe. Yeye huwafanya wawe mwili mmoja. Kutawanyika hakuna baraka, bali huleta taabu, maumivu, kazi ngumu, na majeraha. Hakuna baraka katika kutengana. Lakini mpango wa Mungu unaleta baraka.

4) Sio ndoa yenye mzigo usio sawa.

"Msifunge mnyororo wenye uzito tofauti pamoja na wasiokuwa waaminifu: kwa maana kuna nini mahusiano ya haki na uasi?" (2 Wakorintho 6:14-15). "Mke ameazimwa sheria anapoishi mume wake; lakini mume akiishi, yeye yuko huru kuolewa kwa nani atataka; ila katika Bwana peke yake" (1 Wakorintho 7:39).

Mpango wa Mungu ni kwamba ndoa iwe mzigo sawa. Mungu hatamleta Hawa kwa Adamu katika ndoa ambayo ni mzigo usio sawa. Tufikirie kuacha na kushikamana, kuungana kwa gundi, na wawili wakawa mwili mmoja. Katika ndoa, wawili hao sasa ni mmoja mbele ya Mungu. Fikiria kuwa katika ndoa mbaya kama hii — familia kama hii ikijaribu kufanya kazi pamoja. Hakutakuwa na baraka.

Lakini mzigo sawa unaleta baraka! Mungu anataka tuungane mwili mmoja, mioyo moja, na mawazo moja. Anataka tuonekane tumeungana katika moyo, akili, na mwili—mwenendo mzima, kuwa mmoja. Mpango wa Mungu unaleta baraka.

5) Mungu alikusudia sisi tuwe na watoto.

"Mungu akawaibariki, akawaambia, Uwe wenye matunda, uzidisheni, mkomholee nchi, mkiitawale; na mlikuwa na mamlaka juu ya samaki wa bahari, na ndege wa angani, na kila kiumbe hai kinachotembea juu ya nchi" (Mwanzo 1:28). Fikiria furaha na muujiza kila mara mtoto mwingine akizaliwa katika nyumbani wa Kikristo. Mungu alipanga hivyo. Na kama Mungu alimletea Adamu Hawa yake, na wao wakiacha na kushikamana, wakawa mwili mmoja, moyo mmoja, akili moja. Ikiwa wameyumbishwa sawa na Mungu akawabariki kwa watoto, inakuwa kimbilio cha furaha ambacho Mungu anaweza kukaa ndani yake. "Mungu akamwibariki Nuhu na wanawe, na akawaambia, Uwe wenye matunda, uzidisheni, mkomholee nchi" (Mwanzo 9:1). "Na ninyi, uwe watunze mazao; mnenelee wengi, uzidisheni duniani, mnaishiyo pamoja" (Mwanzo 9:7). Mpango wa Mungu unaleta baraka.

6) Mfuatano wa uongozi (kiongozi wa nyumba).

"Lakini nataka mpate kujua, kwamba kichwa cha kila mwanaume ni Kristo; na kichwa cha mwanamke ni mwanaume; na kichwa cha Kristo ni Mungu" (1 Wakorintho 11:3). Ni Mungu, kisha Kristo, mwanaume, na mwanamke. Mungu aliacha mfuatano wa uongozi, na mfuatano huu wa uongozi ni baraka. Huo ni mpango wa Mungu, na ni baraka.

"Watoto, mtii wazazi wenu katika Bwana: kwa maana hii ni haki. Heshimu baba yako na mama yako; hii ndiyo amri ya kwanza yenye ahadi; ili ikawa vyema kwako, na uwe na maisha marefu juu ya nchi" (Efe. 6:1-3). Watoto, mtii wazazi wenu katika Bwana ni sehemu ya mfuatano wa uongozi. Si vigumu kuelewa, sivyo? Nyumba inayoifuata mpango wa Mungu ni hali yenye baraka. Vijana jifunze kuwa chini ya mamlaka. Ifanye hili kuwa kipaumbele chako. Mapema unavyojifunza kuwa chini ya mamlaka, ndivyo utakavyokuwa umeandaliwa vyema kwa majukumu ya maisha.

Nakumbuka nilipotazama maisha ya ndoa na kuwa na matarajio ya kufundisha watoto na kulea familia takatifu. Nilisikia mfululizo wa "Nyumba Takatifu" na nikadhani nilikuwa tayari. Lakini siku ikafika ilipokuwa zamu yangu na jukumu langu, ghafla moyo wangu ulikuja kubebwa na hofu. Uwajibikaji hauhisi kama kutota kuhusu ndoto tu. WEWE unahitaji kufanya kitu! WEWE una jukumu. WEWE unahitaji kulitenda. Na, kwa njia, si tu kulitenda; unahitaji kulitenda kwa njia ya Kikristo. Unahitaji kulitenda kwa njia ambayo mafuta ya Roho wa Mungu yanaweza kushuka juu ya familia yako. Kadri tunavyojifunza jinsi ya kuwa chini ya mamlaka, ndivyo tutakavyokuwa tumeandaliwa vyema kwa wajibu huo. Kadri tunavyoelewa tunamhitaji Mungu, ndivyo tutakavyoendelea vizuri. Tufanye kipaumbele cha juu kujifunza kuwa chini ya mamlaka kama watoto na kama vijana. "Mwana wangu, usisahau sheria zangu; bali moyo wako uweke amri zangu: kwa vile siku nyingi na maisha marefu, na amani, zitakuongezea" (Mithali 3:1-2).

Mungu ataongeza baraka zake kama tukibaki katika mfuatano huu wa uongozi. Kadri unavyojifunza kuwa chini ya mamlaka, ndivyo utakavyobarikiwa unapojenga nyumba yako. Mpango wa Mungu una baraka.

7) Ndoa takatifu.

Efezo 5:21,22,24 inasema, "Mtieni wenyewe mmoja kwa mwingine kwa hofu ya Mungu. Wake, mtawanyeni wake zenu kama kwa Bwana... Kwa hiyo kama kanisa linamtii Kristo, vivyo hivyo wake wawe kwa wake zao kwa kila jambo."

Kwanza angalia aya ya 21, "mtieni wenyewe mmoja kwa mwingine." Kuna muunganiko unaotakiwa kutokea katika nyumba takatifu. Muunganiko huu unapaswa kutokea kwa hofu ya Mungu. Ikiwa tunajiweka chini ya wenzao kwa hofu ya Mungu, tutamtii Mungu kwa sababu tunataka baraka Zake.

Efezo 5:22,24 "Wake, mtawanyeni wake zenu kama kwa Bwana... Kwa hiyo kama kanisa linamtii Kristo, vivyo hivyo wake wawe kwa wake zao kwa kila jambo." Wasichana wenzangu, mnaweza kutegemea hili: utii kwa Baba ni sawa na utii kwa mume. Unaweza kujaribu wakati uko single. Hii itasaidia kujenga tabia katika maisha yako. Kuwa mwanamke mpotovu na mwasi haitaleta baraka za Mungu.

Inaendelea na kusema, katika Efezo 5:25,28,29. "Wake, wapendeni wake zenu, kama Kristo alivyopenda kanisa, naye akajitoa kwa ajili yake... Vivyo hivyo waume wanapaswa kupenda wake zao kama miili yao. Yeye ampeye mke wake hupenda nafsi yake. Kwa maana hakuna mtu aliyechukia mwili wake mwenyewe bali hupulizia na kumtunza, kama Bwana anavyotenda kwa kanisa." Vijana wa kiume, aya hizi zinatueleza kuwa waume wanapaswa kupenda wake zao. Basi unadhani Mungu aliweka nani katika maisha yako kukuwezesha kujifunza kupenda mke wako? Mama yako! Unataka kujifunza jinsi ya kumpenda mke wako? Jifunze kuishi kwa amani na mama yako, mpe upendo mama yako, na muangalie. Unataka kufanya mazoezi ya kumpenda mke wako wa baadaye? Endelea mpe upendo mama yako.

Aya 33, "Lakini kila mmoja wenu hasa ampende mke wake kama nafsi yake; na mke amheshimu mume yake." Mpango wa Mungu unaleta baraka.

8) Kuwa warithi pamoja neema ya uzima.

1 Petro 3:7 "Vivyo hivyo ninyi waume, muishi nao kwa busara, mkiwapa heshima wake kama vazi dhaifu, kama warithi pamoja wa neema ya uzima; ili sala zenu zisizuilike." Kama waume, tunamwonyesha mke heshima. Yeye ndiye vazi dhaifu na ndiye aliyebeba watoto! Amepitia mabadiliko mengi ya mshtuko maishani. Yeye ndiye anayechoka mapema zaidi.

Na anasema, "Waume, muishi nao kwa busara."

Vijana wa kiume, jifunze kumtelewa mama yako na dada zako. Itakusaidia baada ya kuoa. Usiwachee kwa dhana, ah, hao ni wanawake tu. Hapana, unataka baraka za Mungu. Jifunze kuwajua na kuwaelewa.

"Warithi pamoja wa neema ya uzima." Mungu anataka tuwe warithi pamoja wa neema ya uzima. Ikiwa hatuwezi kuwa warithi pamoja wa neema ya uzima, je, tunaweza kuwa warithi waliosambazwa wa neema ya uzima? Sidhani hivyo. Anasema tunapaswa kuwa warithi pamoja ili sala zetu zisizuilike. Hivyo kama tuko warithi wakitengwa, tunaweza kusema sala zetu zitaingiliwa? Ndiyo, sala zetu zitaingiliwa. Tumpaie heshima mke kama vazi dhaifu. Kiasi kila unachoweza kupata katika eneo hili kitakuibarikia baadaye. Inastahili. Mpango wa Mungu unaleta baraka.

9) Nyumba iliyoibarikiwa na salama.

Hii inatokana kwa sehemu na 1 Petro 3:7, lakini pia kutoka Zaburi 144:12 "Ili wana wetu wawe kama mimea iliyokomaa ujana wao; ili binti zetu ziwe kama jiwe la pembe la pembe, zilizoshonwa kama mfano wa jumba." Neema ya Mungu iko katika nyumba iliyo salama ambapo kuna umoja. Ambapo Baba anamtambua Mama, ambapo Baba anamjali Mama. Baba anahudumiana na yupo kusaidia na kuongoza. Yupo kutoa mwelekeo kwa moyo wa huruma. Mpango wa Mungu kwa mwanaume na mwanamke—mpango wa Mungu unaleta baraka.

10) Kama Kristo na kanisa.

"Kwa hiyo kama kanisa linamtii Kristo, vivyo hivyo wake wawe kwa wake zao kwa kila jambo. Waume, wapendeni wake zenu, kama Kristo alivyopenda kanisa, naye akajitoa kwa ajili yake; Ili amtakase na kuisafisha kwa kuoga kwa maji kwa neno; Ili amtuletee mwenyewe kanisa lenye utukufu, lisilo na doa wala mkomo, wala kitu kama hicho; bali liwe takatifu na lisilo na doa. Vivyo hivyo waume wanapaswa kupenda wake zao kama miili yao. Yeye ampeye mke wake hupenda nafsi yake. Kwa maana hakuna mtu aliyechukia mwili wake mwenyewe bali hupulizia na kumtunza, kama Bwana anavyofanya kwa kanisa" (Efezo 5:24-29).

"Waume, wapendeni wake zenu, kama Kristo alivyopenda kanisa, naye akajitoa kwa ajili yake." Mungu anatafuta wanaume walioko tayari kutoa maisha yao. Vijana wenzangu wasioolewa/wasiooeshwa, mnaotaka kujibu wito na kutoa maisha yenu? Huu ni wito mkuu wa Mungu. Ni mpango wa Mungu.

Vijana wa kiume, mko tayari kuweka maisha yenu, ratiba zenu, na mambo yale ya kujitegemea mnapenda kufanya? Mko tayari kuwa wavumilivu, wavumilivu kwa upole, na waelewa? Mko tayari kupoteza usingizi na kuendelea hata mkiwa mnachoka? Mko tayari kubaki mtulivu na kutojibu kwa msongo wa mawazo? Mko tayari kuongoza na kuwaongoza mke na watoto, nafsi za milele, kupitia maisha haya?

Lakini kilio changu ni kwamba wangesema, "Niko tayari nijivike kwa Neno la Mungu, mapenzi ya Mungu, mpango wa Mungu, na nitatupa maisha yangu. Niko tayari kuyafanya ofrenda." Yesu alitoa maisha yake kwa ajili yetu, na Yeye analinganisha ndoa na kanisa na Yeye mwenyewe.

Pia kuna haja ya wake ambao wako watii na wameyenyekea kwa mamlaka. Wake ambao hawafuati uzalendo wa wanawake wa wakati wetu bali walionekana kuridhika kuwa wakahifadhi wa nyumbani.

Wasichana, mko tayari kujiandikisha? Mtawapa moyo mioyo yenu kuongozwa na kupewa maelekezo? Mko tayari kumfuata na kwa furaha kujiweka chini ya mamlaka yenu? Mko tayari kuhudumia na kujitoa kwa ajili ya familia yenu? Mko tayari kuhudumia na kujitoa kwa ajili ya FAMILIA YENU? Ukioa siku moja, itakuwa FAMILIA YENU mnayohudumia na kujitoa kwa ajili yake. Mko tayari kubeba maumivu na kutokuwa na faraja? Mko tayari kuwa msaada mwafaa, kujitoa kwa ajili ya mzigo na maono yake?

Lakini tunapotazama mpango wa Mungu na baraka zake, mnataka baraka za Mungu, vijana! Lakini hiyo inamaanisha mnahitaji kufanya maamuzi ipasavyo. Inuka na yafanye maamuzi yatakayosababisha ukuaji. Ukuaji unakuja katika mchakato wa kumtafuta Mungu. Fanya ahadi moyoni mwako kujifungulia kwa baraka na kanuni za Mungu. Nawahimiza kutembea na Mungu, kuwa na uhusiano na Yesu Kristo, na kufanya hivyo kwa unyenyekevu.

Mtafuta tabia ya Kikristo, na fanya kwa kusudi. Ni rahisi sana kwetu kuishi maisha bila mpangilio. Lakini tukifanya maamuzi kwa kusudi, yatatufikisha mahali! Maamuzi hayo ni muhimu. Fanya mambo kwa mujibu wa mpango wa Mungu.

Mungu ana mpango kwa mwanaume na mwanamke na ana mpango kwako.

“Dr. Waldron, Elsie needs help!” Elsie’s husband was adamant, almost angry, as he stared at me. On the other hand, Elsie stared at the floor, almost as though she wasn’t present. I had never met either of the couple before and was struggling just a little to figure out what was needed from me to help her.

“What is going on?” I asked as I flipped through her chart. This was still in the days of paper charts, and I headed to the lab section of her chart. There wasn’t anything too crazy that I could see there—her liver enzymes were a little elevated, but otherwise, everything seemed OK.

“It’s her drinking!” Her husband told me. “She is drinking more and more every night. She won’t go out except to get whiskey. She drinks till she passes out every night and has to have something every morning to get her started.”

“Is that true?” I asked Elsie, feeling like a judge overseeing a jury trial.

“Yes,” she said. Her face was emotionless, and I couldn’t tell if she wanted to be there or not.

“Do you want help?” I asked her. This was a loaded question. Many people who struggle with alcoholism aren’t ready to break free from its vice-like hold on them. Maybe Elsie was different.

“I guess so,” she said, indifferently. Once again, I couldn’t tell whether she wanted to be there or not.

“At the rate at which you are drinking, you will kill yourself within a year – maybe two at best – if you don’t give up alcohol entirely,” I told her. “If you want to, I will try to find you an inpatient program to detox you and get you off of alcohol.”

“She’s ready,” he husband said firmly.

When dealing with someone who drinks heavily, it is crucial that they don’t simply stop drinking without medical support. Abrupt cessation of alcohol use causes the body to go into withdrawal which can produce a state called Delirium Tremens and even seizures.

I stepped out of the exam room and to make phone calls. It is never easy to find a place for someone to attempt to rehabilitate from any kind of substances, and it was over an hour and a half before I found a facility that was willing to take Elsie and try to help her get off of the whiskey.

I sighed as I reentered her exam room. I had been afraid that I wouldn’t find anywhere for her to go.

I told them about the plan, and her husband nodded vigorously, while Elise continued to stare silently at the floor. “Can we pray together before you go?” I asked them, and when they nodded assent, I prayed with them, asking for freedom and Jesus’ presence in both of their lives.

They left my office with marching orders and directions on where to go. I had a happy glow about me for the rest of the morning, knowing that I had gone the extra mile and had really made a difference in this middle-aged couple’s life.

Around 2 pm, I got a call from the rehab facility. They hadn’t seen even a shadow of Elsie or her husband, which was surprising, since it was a bright sunny day and the facility wasn’t that far away. With a sinking feeling, I dialed the couple’s phone number.

“She won’t go!” Her husband told me. “She tells me that she told me this ahead of time. She’ll try to cut back, but she isn’t willing to go into a rehab facility or any such thing. I guess just tell them that we’ll let them know if she changes her mind.”

My nurse called the rehab facility and told them the bad news, and I sat down in my chair, stunned. What else could I have done? Was there a solution for Elsie—something different that I could have said that would have made a difference in her life?

About a year later, I received the sad news that Elsie had died at home. I was certain that things would have been different if she had gone to rehab and if she had given control to Jesus. None of that had happened, and I felt cynicism pushing into my heart.

Cynicism

We live in an age of cynicism. In ancient Greece, the cynics were an odd assortment of men who specialized in being grouchy and saying mean (they would have said truthful) things to people. They often dressed in rags and behaved in such a way that most of the polite Athenians did not want to be close to them.

Today, cynicism means a tendency to believe the worst about people and circumstances. Cynical people believe that all people are motivated purely by selfishness and that bad events will tend to prevail.

Many young doctors are idealistic and very hopeful. They believe that if they exert the utmost effort, they can make a real, positive impact on their patient’s lives. Unfortunately, as time goes by and they try their hardest and their patients don’t change, they can give up. These doctors still try, but they no longer really hope that their efforts will make much of a difference.

It seems as though people who get involved with politics often have the best of intentions. They see this as a path to changing society for the better. Unfortunately, as time goes by and the faces in charge change, the policies don’t really change, they tend to become cynical.

Sometimes this cynicism is directed against all politicians. Sometimes it is only anger directed against members of the party that opposes their party’s positions. Hope is replaced by cynicism.

Cynicism in the Bible

If there is a book in the Bible that seems to have been written by a cynical man, it is the book of Ecclesiastes. The Preacher, who we understand to be Solomon, lists all of the things that he endeavored in an attempt to find joy.

In chapter 2:17-23 Solomon describes work as futile. He finishes by saying, “For what hath man of all his labour, and of the vexation of his heart, wherein he hath laboured under the sun? For all his days are sorrows, and his travail grief; yea, his heart taketh not rest in the night. This is also vanity.” (Ecclesiastes 2:22,23)

He saw the world as being dominated by tyrants and there was little that the people could do about it. Solomon went so far as to say that political power was meaningless “Better is a poor and a wise child than an old and foolish king, who will no more be admonished. For out of prison he cometh to reign; whereas also he that is born in his kingdom becometh poor” (Ecclesiastes 4:13).

In Ecclesiastes 6:6, he seems to disparage long life. “Yea, though he live a thousand years twice told, yet hath he seen no good: do not all go to one place?”

Of course, he finishes his short book with the instruction to remember our Creator in the days of our youth. There is a blessing for those who choose to focus on God when they have a little bit of energy left and not, when they are old and jaded, like Solomon.

Later on, it almost seemed as though God had given up on His people. He still sent prophets to them, but He knew without a doubt that the people would refuse to respond. “Therefore thou shalt speak all these words unto them; but they will not hearken to thee: thou shalt also call unto them; but they will not answer thee” (Jeremiah 7:27).

Even in the New Testament, Paul told Timothy that the time was coming when people would no longer listen to sound doctrine. “For the time will come when they will not endure sound doctrine; but after their own lusts shall they heap to themselves teachers, having itching ears;” (2 Timothy 4:3).

By picking and choosing these passages, we can come away with a very gloomy view of the future and, more specifically, of human’s willingness to change. It seems there is little point of investing ourselves in the people around us. They are full of woe and are as likely to change as a chipmunk is to master differential calculus.

The Opposite of Cynicism

The opposite of cynicism is hope. It is the belief that the future could be better.

It is interesting that the Apostle Paul spoke of tribulations in the Epistle to the Romans, “And not only so, but we glory in tribulations also: knowing that tribulation worketh patience; and patience, experience; and experience, hope: and hope maketh not ashamed; because the love of God is shed abroad in our hearts by the Holy Ghost which is given unto us” (Romans 5:3-5).

We may not have reached the place where we glory in the trials we experience, but certainly, they should bring us these other things that he mentions. For, we grow in patience and experience, even as we deal with trials, but more than that, we come to realize that we have hope for tomorrow because we serve a great God.

The contrast in the story of the Prodigal Son in Luke 15 teaches us much about hope. The father and the older brother were strikingly different in their attitudes.

The father had never given up hope – he knew that his son had failed him and gone far from what he knew was right and yet, the father still desired to see the prodigal come to himself and return home.

On the other hand, the older brother not only had no hope for his younger brother, but he was also angry with him. The prodigal had wasted his money, he had lived in sin, and now, he had returned home just because he was out of money.

Certainly, there was no reason to trust the younger son. Yet, that is exactly what our Heavenly Father does for us.

Look for Hope in the Right Places

Part of the problem is that we look for hope in the wrong places. A number of years ago, a presidential candidate ran for office under the slogan “Hope and Change,” and yet, even though he was elected, I imagine most folks did not feel that their lives were significantly changed for the better.

Pursuing the things this world values—political power and wealth is guaranteed to bring emptiness. This is Satan’s pattern—he always over-promises and under-delivers.

This was what he did when he tempted Jesus, “All these things will I give thee, if thou wilt fall down and worship me” (Matthew 4:8). All of the things Satan offered, nothing compared with the glory that Jesus eventually received from the road that led to the cross.

In the same way, Satan would like to distract Christians from seeking the things that are valuable, and that will bring hope. Satan tells Christians that politics will not only change the world for the better, it is an easier way to change the world.

The Bible is clear that we build hope as we nurture our relationship with God and then work to help our brothers and sisters build that same relationship in their own lives. The reason that we can hope is not because people are so wonderful—we don’t have to live very long to realize that they aren’t. The reason we hope is because we serve an awesome, faithful God who walks with us through the worst of our trials.

Remember that We Have Undeserved Hope

Jesus’ messages about forgiveness make it clear that one of the major reasons that we have for forgiving others in our lives is that we have received great and undeserved forgiveness. The same is true for hope.

Each one of us was hopeless and without reason to expect to receive hope and we were still given a ray of light in the midst of our darkness. Maybe part of the reason that we have so much trouble hoping for good things for the people around us is that we do not remember how hopeless we were before we found grace.

If Jesus was able to bring hope to our hopeless existence, then certainly He can do wonderful things in the hearts and lives of others around us. The only people we should give up on are the ones that our Savior has given up on as well.

Small Efforts Do Make a Difference

I remember having a conversation with a young person who was planning to go into medicine and had a plan to go to a foreign country and serve the people there. As we were talking, an older man entered the conversation and shared that he saw little hope for change in developing countries.

The people in those countries just weren’t interested in getting better and didn’t do the minimum necessary to stave off things like worms and parasites. Doctors and nurses couldn’t make a difference in such an environment.

I could sense the heart of the youth sinking as this older man shared. He had experience, and he had given up hope. The sad thing was that he was also stealing the hope of someone who still had a desire to serve.

When I was in training, I had a surgeon tell me that family doctors didn’t really do anything. They simply kept their patients alive till their next office visit, whereas surgeons really “fixed” people—taking out (or off) the offending body part.

At the end of the day, small efforts do make a difference. I don’t do brain surgery, but I still can make a difference in someone else’s life— maybe just by spending a little time and listening and praying. This is true for all of us.

More than that, we come to realize that making this effort changes our own lives for the better. Jesus told the sheep that as they ministered to “the least of these my brethren,” they were ministering to Him.

Even if no one’s life is improved, our Savior knows our desires and feels our efforts, and will reward them someday.

A Few Things to Remember

When we face failures, we tend to move in one of two directions. Those of us who are optimists tend to believe that this episode was an isolated event and that the future is still bright. On the other hand, pessimists believe that failures are permanent, personal, and pervasive.

Pessimists believe that their failures are the result of intrinsic character flaws that they have and that these things affect all of their lives and are unlikely to change. Unlike the righteous man who falls to rise again, these people fall and lie where they fall, defeated at the outset.

When we are dealing with other people, we need to give them the same grace that we should give ourselves. They, too, are growing, and if they have a failure today, they will do better tomorrow. Maybe they will fail again, but they will at least “fail better.”

Conclusion

Cynicism is rife in our world. Many have given up hope for a better future, and it is understandable for those who have invested their hope in this world’s institutions. There is no real hope in government or in armies or in bureaucracy.

The song says, “Oh to have no hope in Jesus, how dark this world must be!” For, Jesus is the one who brings light into our darkness and allows us to continue, even when others fail us.

God is the one who redeems us. He is the one who sent the prophets, even though their messages were ignored, and the prophets were persecuted. He is the one who continues to hope for us, even when we have failed Him so many times in the past.

He is the reason we carry on. He is the reason that we have hope, not only for ourselves but also for our brothers.

„Dr. Waldron, Elsie braucht Hilfe!“ Elsies Ehemann war bestimmt, fast wütend, als er mich anstarrte. Auf der anderen Seite starrte Elsie auf den Boden, fast so, als wäre sie nicht anwesend. Ich hatte das Paar zuvor noch nie getroffen und bemühte mich ein wenig herauszufinden, was von mir gebraucht wurde, um ihr zu helfen.

„Was ist los?“ fragte ich, während ich ihre Akte durchblätterte. Das war noch in den Zeiten der Papierakten, und ich ging zum Laborbereich ihrer Akte. Dort war nichts allzu Auffälliges zu sehen – ihre Leberwerte waren ein wenig erhöht, aber ansonsten schien alles in Ordnung zu sein.

„Es ist ihr Trinken!“ sagte ihr Ehemann. „Sie trinkt jede Nacht mehr und mehr. Sie geht nirgendwohin, außer um Whiskey zu holen. Sie trinkt sich jede Nacht zu Tode und muss jeden Morgen etwas haben, um in den Tag zu kommen.“

„Ist das wahr?“ fragte ich Elsie, und fühlte mich dabei wie ein Richter, der eine Jury befragt.

„Ja,“ sagte sie. Ihr Gesicht zeigte keine Emotion, und ich konnte nicht erkennen, ob sie dort sein wollte oder nicht.

„Willst du Hilfe?“ fragte ich sie. Das war eine schwierige Frage. Viele Menschen, die mit Alkoholismus ringen, sind nicht bereit, sich aus seinem griffartigen Einfluss zu befreien. Vielleicht war Elsie anders.

„Ich denke schon,“ sagte sie gleichgültig. Wieder konnte ich nicht sagen, ob sie dort sein wollte oder nicht.

„In dem Tempo, wie du trinkst, wirst du dich innerhalb eines Jahres – vielleicht bestenfalls innerhalb von zwei Jahren – umbringen, wenn du nicht völlig auf Alkohol verzichtest,“ sagte ich ihr. „Wenn du willst, werde ich versuchen, ein stationäres Programm für dich zu finden, um dich zu entgiften und vom Alkohol wegzubringen.“

„Sie ist bereit,“ sagte ihr Ehemann entschieden.

Wenn man es mit jemandem zu tun hat, der stark trinkt, ist es entscheidend, dass diese Person nicht einfach ohne medizinische Unterstützung mit dem Trinken aufhört. Ein abruptes Stilllegen des Alkoholkonsums bringt den Körper in einen Entzug, der einen Zustand namens Delirium tremens und sogar Krampfanfälle hervorrufen kann.

Ich trat aus dem Untersuchungszimmer und begann, Anrufe zu tätigen. Es ist nie einfach, einen Platz für jemanden zu finden, der versucht, sich von irgendeiner Art von Substanzen zu rehabilitieren, und es dauerte über eineinhalb Stunden, bis ich eine Einrichtung fand, die bereit war, Elsie aufzunehmen und zu versuchen, ihr beim Entzug vom Whiskey zu helfen.

Ich seufzte, als ich zurück in ihr Untersuchungszimmer kam. Ich hatte befürchtet, dass ich keinen Platz für sie finden würde.

Ich erklärte ihnen den Plan, und ihr Ehemann nickte eifrig, während Elsie weiterhin stumm auf den Boden starrte. „Können wir zusammen beten, bevor Sie gehen?“ fragte ich sie, und als sie zustimmten, betete ich mit ihnen und bat um Befreiung und Jesu Gegenwart in ihrem beider Leben.

Sie verließen mein Büro mit klaren Anweisungen und Wegbeschreibungen. Ich hatte den Rest des Morgens ein glückliches Gefühl, weil ich wusste, dass ich die Extra-Meile gegangen war und wirklich einen Unterschied im Leben dieses mittelalten Paares gemacht hatte.

Gegen 14:00 Uhr erhielt ich einen Anruf von der Reha-Einrichtung. Sie hatten weder Elsie noch ihren Ehemann gesehen, was überraschend war, da es ein heller, sonniger Tag war und die Einrichtung nicht so weit entfernt war. Mit einem sinkenden Gefühl wählte ich die Telefonnummer des Paares.

„Sie will nicht gehen!“ sagte ihr Ehemann. „Sie sagt, sie hätte mir das vorher gesagt. Sie wird versuchen, weniger zu trinken, aber sie ist nicht bereit, in eine Reha-Einrichtung oder so etwas zu gehen. Ich denke, sagen Sie ihnen einfach, wir werden uns melden, wenn sie ihre Meinung ändert.“

Meine Krankenschwester rief die Reha-Einrichtung an und überbrachte die schlechte Nachricht, und ich setzte mich in meinen Stuhl, benommen. Was hätte ich sonst noch tun können? Gab es eine Lösung für Elsie – etwas anderes, das ich hätte sagen können, das einen Unterschied in ihrem Leben gemacht hätte?

Etwa ein Jahr später erhielt ich die traurige Nachricht, dass Elsie zu Hause gestorben sei. Ich war überzeugt, dass es anders gekommen wäre, wenn sie zur Reha gegangen und wenn sie die Kontrolle an Jesus abgegeben hätte. Nichts davon war geschehen, und ich spürte, wie Zynismus in mein Herz eindrang.

Zynismus

Wir leben in einem Zeitalter des Zynismus. Im antiken Griechenland waren die Kyniker eine seltsame Schar von Männern, die darauf spezialisiert waren, mürrisch zu sein und gemeine (sie hätten gesagt: wahrhaftige) Dinge zu den Leuten zu sagen. Sie kleideten sich oft in Lumpen und verhielten sich so, dass die meisten höflichen Athener nicht in ihrer Nähe sein wollten.

Heute bedeutet Zynismus eine Neigung, das Schlimmste über Menschen und Umstände zu glauben. Zynische Menschen glauben, dass alle Menschen ausschließlich von Eigeninteresse motiviert sind und dass schlechte Ereignisse sich durchsetzen werden.

Viele junge Ärztinnen und Ärzte sind idealistisch und sehr hoffnungsvoll. Sie glauben, dass sie, wenn sie sich außerordentlich anstrengen, einen echten, positiven Einfluss auf das Leben ihrer Patienten ausüben können. Leider kann es mit der Zeit, wenn sie ihr Bestes geben und ihre Patienten sich nicht ändern, dazu kommen, dass sie aufgeben. Diese Ärzte versuchen es weiterhin, aber sie hoffen nicht mehr wirklich, dass ihre Anstrengungen viel bewirken werden.

Es scheint, als würden Menschen, die sich in die Politik einbringen, oft die besten Absichten haben. Sie sehen darin einen Weg, die Gesellschaft zum Besseren zu verändern. Leider neigen sie im Lauf der Zeit, wenn die Gesichter an der Spitze wechseln und die Politik sich nicht wirklich ändert, dazu, zynisch zu werden.

Manchmal richtet sich dieser Zynismus gegen alle Politiker. Manchmal ist es nur Wut gegen Mitglieder der Partei, die gegen die eigene Partei steht. Hoffnung wird durch Zynismus ersetzt.

Zynismus in der Bibel

Wenn es ein Buch in der Bibel gibt, das von einem zynischen Mann geschrieben zu sein scheint, dann ist es das Buch Kohelet. Der Prediger, den wir als Salomo verstehen, listet all die Dinge auf, die er unternahm, um Freude zu finden.

In Kapitel 2:17-23 beschreibt Salomo Arbeit als vergeblich. Er schließt mit den Worten: „Denn was hat der Mensch von all seiner Mühe und von all dem Ärger seines Herzens, womit er sich unter der Sonne abmüht? Denn alle seine Tage sind Sorge, und seine Arbeit ist Schmerz; ja, sein Herz findet des Nachts keine Ruhe. Das ist auch eine Eitelkeit.“ (Kohelet 2:22,23)

Er sah die Welt als von Tyrannen beherrscht an, und die Menschen konnten wenig dagegen tun. Salomo ging so weit zu sagen, dass politische Macht bedeutungslos sei: „Besser ist ein armes und weises Kind denn ein alter und törichter König, der nicht mehr ermahnt wird. Denn aus dem Gefängnis kommt er, um zu herrschen; und des Königs Sohn, der in seinem Reich geboren wird, wird arm.“ (Kohelet 4:13)

In Kohelet 6:6 scheint er ein langes Leben zu verachten: „Ja, wenn er tausend Jahre lebte und noch einmal tausend, und sah doch kein Gut: gehen sie nicht alle an einen Ort?“

Natürlich schließt er sein kurzes Buch mit der Anweisung, den Schöpfer in den Tagen der Jugend zu gedenken. Es gibt einen Segen für diejenigen, die sich entscheiden, Gott zu suchen, wenn sie noch etwas Energie haben und nicht, wenn sie alt und verbraucht sind, wie Salomo.

Später schien es beinahe so, als hätte Gott sein Volk aufgegeben. Er sandte zwar weiterhin Propheten zu ihnen, wusste aber ohne Zweifel, dass das Volk sich weigern würde zu antworten: „Darum sollst du ihnen alle diese Worte sagen; sie werden aber nicht auf dich hören; und du sollst zu ihnen rufen, sie werden dir auch nicht antworten.“ (Jeremia 7:27)

Sogar im Neuen Testament sagte Paulus zu Timotheus, dass die Zeit kommen werde, da die Menschen nicht mehr auf gesunde Lehre hören würden: „Denn es wird eine Zeit sein, da sie die gesunde Lehre nicht ertragen werden; sondern nach ihren eigenen Begierden werden sie sich Lehrer haben, die ihnen in die Ohren kitzeln.“ (2 Timotheus 4:3)

Wenn wir diese Stellen auswählen und herauspicken, können wir mit einer sehr düsteren Sicht auf die Zukunft und speziell auf die Bereitschaft der Menschen, sich zu ändern, zurückbleiben. Es scheint wenig Sinn zu machen, uns in die Menschen um uns herum zu investieren. Sie sind voll von Weh und so wahrscheinlich, sich zu ändern, wie ein Streifenhörnchen Differentialrechnung zu beherrschen.

Das Gegenteil von Zynismus

Das Gegenteil von Zynismus ist Hoffnung. Es ist der Glaube, dass die Zukunft besser sein könnte.

Es ist interessant, dass der Apostel Paulus in seinem Brief an die Römer von Trübsalen sprach: „Nicht allein aber das, sondern wir rühmen uns auch in den Trübsalen; wissend, dass Trübsal Geduld wirkt; Geduld aber Bewährung; Bewährung aber Hoffnung; die Hoffnung aber lässt nicht zuschanden werden; denn die Liebe Gottes ist ausgegossen in unsere Herzen durch den Heiligen Geist, der uns gegeben ist.“ (Römer 5:3-5)

Vielleicht sind wir noch nicht an dem Punkt, wo wir uns in den Prüfungen rühmen, die wir erfahren, aber sicherlich sollten diese Dinge, die er erwähnt, in uns wachsen. Denn wir wachsen in Geduld und Bewährung, wenn wir mit Prüfungen umgehen, und mehr noch: Wir erkennen, dass wir Hoffnung für das Morgen haben, weil wir einem großen Gott dienen.

Der Gegensatz in der Geschichte vom verlorenen Sohn in Lukas 15 lehrt uns viel über Hoffnung. Vater und älterer Sohn unterschieden sich auffallend in ihrer Haltung.

Der Vater hatte niemals die Hoffnung aufgegeben – er wusste, dass sein Sohn ihn enttäuscht hatte und weit von dem Weg abgekommen war, den er für richtig hielt, und doch wünschte der Vater sich, dass der Verlorene zu sich selbst käme und heimkehrte.

Der ältere Bruder hingegen hatte nicht nur keine Hoffnung für seinen jüngeren Bruder, sondern er war auch zornig auf ihn. Der Verlorene hatte sein Geld verschwendet, in Sünde gelebt, und kehrte nun heim, nur weil ihm das Geld ausgegangen war.

Sicherlich gab es keinen Grund, dem jüngeren Sohn zu vertrauen. Und doch ist genau das, was unser himmlischer Vater für uns tut.

Hoffnung an den richtigen Orten suchen

Ein Teil des Problems besteht darin, dass wir Hoffnung an den falschen Orten suchen. Vor einigen Jahren trat ein Präsidentschaftskandidat mit dem Slogan „Hoffnung und Wandel“ an, und obwohl er gewählt wurde, glaube ich, dass die meisten Menschen nicht das Gefühl hatten, ihr Leben wäre dadurch wesentlich zum Besseren verändert worden.

Dem nachzujagen, was diese Welt schätzt – politische Macht und Reichtum – führt garantiert zur Leere. Das ist Satans Muster – er verspricht immer zu viel und liefert zu wenig.

So handelte er, als er Jesus versuchte: „Alle diese Reiche will ich dir geben, wenn du niederfällst und mich anbetest.“ (Matthäus 4:8) All das, was Satan anbot, war nichts im Vergleich zur Herrlichkeit, die Jesus schließlich auf dem Weg erhielt, der zum Kreuz führte.

In ähnlicher Weise möchte Satan Christen davon ablenken, die Dinge zu suchen, die wertvoll sind und Hoffnung bringen. Satan sagt den Christen, dass Politik nicht nur die Welt zum Besseren verändern werde, sondern auch ein leichterer Weg sei, die Welt zu ändern.

Die Bibel macht deutlich, dass wir Hoffnung aufbauen, indem wir unsere Beziehung zu Gott pflegen und dann daran arbeiten, unseren Brüdern und Schwestern zu helfen, dieselbe Beziehung in ihrem Leben zu entwickeln. Der Grund, warum wir hoffen können, liegt nicht darin, dass Menschen so wunderbar sind – wir müssen nicht lange leben, um zu erkennen, dass sie es nicht sind. Der Grund, warum wir hoffen, ist, weil wir einem großartigen, treuen Gott dienen, der mit uns durch die schlimmsten unserer Prüfungen geht.

Erinnere dich daran, dass wir unverdiente Hoffnung haben

Jesu Botschaften über Vergebung machen deutlich, dass einer der Hauptgründe, anderen in unserem Leben zu vergeben, darin besteht, dass wir selbst große und unverdiente Vergebung empfangen haben. Gleiches gilt für die Hoffnung.

Jeder von uns war hoffnungslos und hatte keinen Anlass, Hoffnung zu erwarten, und doch wurde uns inmitten unserer Dunkelheit ein Lichtstrahl gegeben. Vielleicht ist ein Teil des Grundes, warum wir so große Schwierigkeiten haben, Gutes für die Menschen um uns herum zu hoffen, dass wir nicht daran denken, wie hoffnungslos wir waren, bevor wir Gnade gefunden haben.

Wenn Jesus Hoffnung in unser hoffnungsloses Dasein bringen konnte, dann kann Er sicherlich Wunder in den Herzen und Leben der Menschen um uns tun. Die einzigen Menschen, auf die wir verzichten sollten, sind diejenigen, auf die auch unser Retter verzichtet hat.

Kleine Anstrengungen bewirken tatsächlich etwas

Ich erinnere mich an ein Gespräch mit einer jungen Person, die Medizin studieren wollte und plante, in ein fremdes Land zu gehen, um dort den Menschen zu dienen. Als wir redeten, kam ein älterer Mann in das Gespräch und teilte mit, dass er wenig Hoffnung auf Veränderung in Entwicklungsländern sähe.

Die Menschen in diesen Ländern wären einfach nicht daran interessiert, sich zu bessern, und täten nicht das Mindeste, um Dinge wie Wurminfektionen und Parasiten vorzubeugen. Ärzte und Krankenschwestern könnten in einer solchen Umgebung keinen Unterschied machen.

Ich spürte, wie das Herz des jungen Menschen sank, als dieser ältere Mann sprach. Er hatte Erfahrung, und er hatte die Hoffnung aufgegeben. Das Traurige daran war, dass er auch die Hoffnung eines Menschen stahl, der noch den Wunsch hatte zu dienen.

Als ich in der Ausbildung war, sagte mir ein Chirurg, dass Hausärzte eigentlich nichts täten. Sie hielten ihre Patienten nur bis zum nächsten Termin am Leben, während Chirurgen wirklich „reparierten“ – das störende Körperteil entfernten.

Am Ende des Tages machen kleine Anstrengungen tatsächlich einen Unterschied. Ich mache keine Hirnoperation, aber ich kann trotzdem das Leben eines anderen verändern – vielleicht einfach, indem ich ein wenig Zeit aufbringe, zuhöre und bete. Das gilt für uns alle.

Mehr noch: Wir erkennen, dass uns diese Anstrengung selbst zum Besseren verändert. Jesus sagte den Schafen, dass sie, wenn sie den „geringsten dieser Brüder“ dienten, ihm dienten.

Selbst wenn niemandes Leben verbessert würde, kennt unser Retter unsere Sehnsüchte, fühlt unsere Anstrengungen und wird sie eines Tages belohnen.

Ein paar Dinge zum Erinnern

Wenn wir mit Misserfolgen konfrontiert sind, neigen wir dazu, uns in eine von zwei Richtungen zu bewegen. Die Optimisten unter uns glauben tendenziell, dass diese Episode ein isoliertes Ereignis war und dass die Zukunft weiterhin hell ist. Andererseits glauben Pessimisten, dass Misserfolge dauerhaft, persönlich und allgegenwärtig sind.

Pessimisten glauben, dass ihre Misserfolge das Ergebnis intrinsischer Charakterfehler sind, die sie haben, und dass diese Dinge alle Bereiche ihres Lebens betreffen und sich kaum ändern werden. Anders als der gerechte Mann, der fällt, um wieder aufzustehen, fallen diese Leute und liegen dort, wo sie gefallen sind, von vornherein besiegt.

Wenn wir es mit anderen Menschen zu tun haben, müssen wir ihnen dieselbe Gnade geben, die wir uns selbst geben sollten. Auch sie wachsen, und wenn sie heute versagen, werden sie es morgen besser machen. Vielleicht versagen sie wieder, aber sie werden zumindest „besser versagen".

Schluss

Zynismus ist in unserer Welt weit verbreitet. Viele haben die Hoffnung auf eine bessere Zukunft aufgegeben, und das ist verständlich für diejenigen, die ihre Hoffnung in die Institutionen dieser Welt gesetzt haben. In Regierung, Armeen oder Bürokratien gibt es keine echte Hoffnung.

Das Lied sagt: „Oh, hätte man keine Hoffnung in Jesus, wie finster müsste diese Welt sein!“ Denn Jesus ist derjenige, der Licht in unsere Dunkelheit bringt und uns weitermachen lässt, selbst wenn andere uns enttäuschen.

Gott ist der, der uns erlöst. Er ist der, der die Propheten sandte, obwohl ihre Botschaften ignoriert wurden und die Propheten verfolgt wurden. Er ist derjenige, der weiterhin Hoffnung für uns hat, selbst wenn wir ihn in der Vergangenheit so oft enttäuscht haben.

Er ist der Grund, warum wir weitermachen. Er ist der Grund, warum wir Hoffnung haben, nicht nur für uns selbst, sondern auch für unsere Brüder.
